title: Disdain Things You Cannot Have: Ignoring Them Is the Best Revenge
coreMove: Starve the unattainable object of attention so it stops defining your status
sourcePressure: Chapter 36 centers on refusing to feed what denies or escapes you with more complaint, chasing, or emotional tribute. The law values disdain and strategic inattention because visible fixation can lower status and enlarge the power of the unattainable object. Its limit is that indifference fails when it becomes fake denial, avoids recoverable reality, or hides continuing dependence under a pose of contempt. Frozen sidecar provides no traceable named anecdote for this chapter; do not fabricate named source anchors.
